runs.hypothesis: In this simulated world, the pull between particles falls off as 1/r², as in Newtonian gravity.

rounds.assessment: No data yet; the hypothesis is plausible but this world's force law may differ from 1/r².
Early analysis suggests acceleration falls roughly as 1/r (n≈1), which would refute the 1/r² hypothesis; a joint fit will quantify this.
Round-1 drops show acceleration falling much more slowly than 1/r² (n roughly 1–1.4), pointing toward refutation. a3 ≈ 0.05–0.06 still needs tightening.
All drops from r = 2, 3 and 6 fit a 1/r force with k ≈ 0.165, so the exponent is n ≈ 1, far outside the 1.8–2.2 range; the 1/r² hypothesis is refuted.

runs.hypothesis: In this simulated world, the pull between particles falls off as 1/r, as in ordinary two-dimensional gravity.

rounds.assessment: No data yet; the 1/r hypothesis is untested.
Accelerations are too small to resolve over t=2. The hypothesis is still untested, and longer runs are under way.

The probe at r=6 barely moves over t=8, giving a6 ≈ 0.002 ± 0.002, which is far below the a3/2 ≈ 0.0085 that 1/r predicts. The r=2 and r=3 trajectories fit a ≈ 0.15/r², so the falloff is close to inverse-square. The 1/r hypothesis is refuted.
